A routing group's intent threshold is its own — intent-sure, configurable per group (#5101) **What's wrong** #5101 (zminds): the confidence an intent rule needs of the classifier's answer was `jevSure`, a compile-time `0.4` fixed for every group. zminds' trace of one day's traffic shows why that's too blunt: of 237 classified turns, 39 — **16.5%** — were refused at 0.4 (sure 0.153–0.395), matched no intent rule, and fell through to the group's default routing, as if the intent rules weren't there. The threshold could not be turned down for a group whose rules you trust. **Root cause** The 0.4 threshold is a compile-time constant in `internal/gateway/decide.go` (`jevSure`), applied inside `readJev` before the group is known, and a group's record (`provider.Group`) has no field to ask its own. **The fix** A group gets its own threshold, `intentSure`: - `provider.Group.IntentSure *float64` — `nil` (the default) keeps the 0.4 groups have always asked, so nothing changes for anyone who doesn't touch it; from `0` (take the likeliest intent however unsure the classifier is) to `1` (certain). Out-of-range values are refused by `SaveGroup` and by `magpie group set`. - `readJev` no longer decides whether an intent came of the answer: it keeps the classifier's likeliest intent as it said it (`Said`, per #4598) with `Sure`, and marks an answer of intents (`Topic`) — a message may be none of those — against an answer of levels (every message is at one of them; a torn pick keeps the turn before's level, as ever). - The group's own sure is applied where the group is known — `ruleFor`, via the new `intentOf`: an answer unsure at the group's sure is no intent, "none of these" is never an intent at any setting, and levels and effort are as they were. The trace keeps the sure and the said either way, so the turn still tells why it went as it did. - Set it in the group editor ("Intent sure", under the classifier), or from a terminal: `magpie group set intent-sure=0.25` (empty restores the default 0.4); said in the intents doc. Patch, `git am` applies it as is (base `upstream/main` `f44fa2ef6`):
patch (git am applies it as is; SHA-256 first 16: c7b5be2597b78e87) ```patch From 96f8821136e59b485f6e14c90f3bd83fd7b31df6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001 From: ggbdpq Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 18:01:05 +0800 Subject: [PATCH] gateway: a routing group's intent threshold is its own (intent-sure configurable) Jev's sure of an intent an intent rule needed was jevSure, a compile-time 0.4 fixed for every group: an unsure pick matched no rule and the turn went by the group's routing as if the intent rules weren't there (zminds #5101: of 237 turns classified one day, 39, 16.5%, were refused at 0.4, sure 0.153 to 0.395, and fell through to the group's default routing). A group can now ask its own sure of Jev: intentSure in the group's record, from 0, its likeliest intent taken however unsure Jev is, to 1, certain. readJev no longer decides whether an intent came of the answer: it keeps Jev's likeliest intent as it said it (Said, #4598), the sure it was of it, and Topic marking an answer of intents (a message may be none of those) against an answer of levels (every message is at one, the torn keeping the level of the turn before). The group's own sure is applied where the group is known, ruleFor (intentOf): an answer unsure at its sure is no intent, "none of these" never one at any setting, and levels and effort are as they were. The trace keeps the sure and the said either way, so the turn still tells why it went as it did. Set in the group editor (Intent sure, under the classifier), from a terminal (magpie group set intent-sure=0.25; empty for the 0.4 groups have always asked), said in the intents doc; a sure out of 0 to 1 is refused (SaveGroup, groups_cli). 0 takes its likeliest however unsure, "none of these" never + counting; empty is the 0.4 groups have always asked), pick= (routing=manual, every request to that one of its models), fast=[,m2…] (the models sent in their vendor's fast mode; Jev's + // likeliest intent is kept in Intent as it said it, and the group's + // own sure of it applied where it is known (intentOf): a chat model's + // answer is already the one of it that counts. + Topic bool Effort string // the reasoning the turn wants; "" when not asked Score float64 // how hard the classifier took the turn to be, from 0 (low) to 3 (xhigh) Sure float64 // how confident Jev was of the intent, from 0 to 1 diff --git a/internal/gateway/decide.go b/internal/gateway/decide.go index 7d95ce39b..432dd06b1 100644 --- a/internal/gateway/decide.go +++ b/internal/gateway/decide.go @@ -29,10 +29,11 @@ import ( "github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/usage" ) -// jevSure is how confident Jev must be of an intent for it to count. -// Confidence runs from 0, every option as likely, to 1, one certain, as -// System One gives it (provider.Confidence), read from the answer's -// probabilities wherever it has them (sureOf). +// jevSure is how confident Jev must be of an intent for it to count, a +// group setting its own (provider.Group.IntentSure). A topic answer unsure +// at the group's sure is no intent. +func intentOf(v verdict, g provider.Group) string { + if !v.Topic { + return v.Intent + } + if v.Sure < sureNeeded(g) || v.Said == noIntent || v.Intent == "" { + return "" + } + return v.Intent +} + // intentNamed is the one of intents named, or "". func intentNamed(intents []string, name string) string { for _, in := range intents { diff --git a/internal/gateway/decide_intentsure_test.go b/internal/gateway/decide_intentsure_test.go new file mode 100644 index 000000000..508853698 --- /dev/null +++ b/internal/gateway/decide_intentsure_test.go @@ -0,0 +1,145 @@ +package gateway + +import ( + "fmt" + "strings" + "testing" + + "github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/provider" +) + +// #5101: the confidence an intent needs of Jev was fixed at 0.4 for every +// group.     • The timeout is global: in Settings → Models → Replies → Intent classifier timeout, choose 8, 15, 30 or 60 seconds. In ~/.config/magpie/settings.json, "classifyTimeout" accepts whole seconds from 1 to 60; 0 or a missing field uses 8. A custom value in that range appears as its own choice in Settings.

    How sure a Jev classifier must be of an intent for it to match is per group: 40% by default, kept in the group’s record as "intentSure" (a number from 0 to 1). Under it, Jev’s likeliest intent matches no rule and the turn goes by the group’s routing as if the intent rules weren’t there — which is the point: raise the intents’ bar and leave it, or lower it to 0.25 to let an unsure pick match, or to 0 to take Jev’s likeliest however unsure it is. "none of these" is no intent at any setting. Set it in the editor, under the classifier: Intent sure; from a terminal, magpie group set <group> intent-sure=0.25 (empty for 0.4 again). Only a Jev classifier answers with a sureness; a classifier asked in words matches as it answers, and ignores this.
